chunks: And what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding the woman whose husband divorces her while she is menstruating, with one menstruation every three months, he said: 'When three months have passed, her waiting period (iddah) is completed; each month is counted for her as one menstruation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a woman who menstruates only once every three months?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal mechanism for calculating the *iddah* (waiting period) of a woman experiencing irregular menstruation (*al-hayd al-mutaghayyir*), establishing that three months constitute the full period with each month legally treated as a single cycle. This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for resolving cases where the standard monthly cycle cannot be reliably observed, ensuring the divorce becomes final only after the prescribed duration elapses. It reflects the practical application of Quranic principles to variable biological conditions, emphasizing legal certainty (*yaqin*) in marital status.
